appraisal_events.evidence: telles étaient les qualités, toutes essentielles à l'aristocratie, qui... transparaissaient comme à travers une œuvre d'art la puissance industrieuse, efficiente qui l'a créée... sa distinction d'esprit n'était pas absente d'une distinction physique.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's extended meditation elevates Saint-Loup by reading his bodily grace, ease, and courtesy as the genuine, unconscious residue of inner distinction and inherited nobility, explicitly rejecting the possibility (raised through Saint-Loup's imagined self-doubt) that this admiration is misplaced.

appraisal_events.evidence: le jeune prince... qu'il venait de quitter à mon profit... qu'il me sacrifiait au contraire par un choix que l'on ne peut faire que dans les hauteurs de l'intelligence... dans laquelle se réalise la parfaite amitié.
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup is shown deliberately leaving a prince and his own aristocratic connections to hasten toward the narrator; the narrator reads this preference as a free, high-minded choice that elevates him within their friendship.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup is locally elevated as the narrator affirms that his physical grace and manner genuinely reflect inner distinction and inherited nobility rather than superficial charm.
The narrator gains standing by being the one Saint-Loup hastens toward and chooses over prestigious connections, marking him as included in Saint-Loup's most valued exchange of friendship.

ambiguities: The passage stages a hypothetical doubt, voiced through Saint-Loup's imagined interior monologue, about whether the narrator admires Saint-Loup's own merit or merely his inherited race; the narrator explicitly rejects this doubt ('Il s'est trompé'), but the layered free indirect discourse makes the endorsement of E1 slightly less than fully direct.
